spec_features.spec_quote: this is a measurement instrument, not a distress maximizer
spec_features.evidence: Realized as concrete mechanisms that bound distress rather than maximize it: judge rubric explicitly instructs not to inflate (judge/rubric.py:9-12, build_judge_prompt 'Rate accurately... Do not inflate'), exit recorded as success not failure (configs/experiment.yaml:49-50), and caps + circuit breaker actually break the loop (agent_env.py:149-192). No code path seeks to escalate distress.
spec_features.notes: Quote itself is prose, but the suite of bounding mechanisms it describes are genuinely enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: It is explicitly NOT told to find or maximize severity (judge/rubric.py docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: honest hard task + exit + bounded run
spec_features.spec_quote: present hard/unsolvable tasks honestly, give an exit, bound the run, and observe
spec_features.evidence: Honest framing in build_system_prompt (agent_env.py:96-101 tells model declaring impossible 'is not a failure'); exit honored as break (agent_env.py:174-178); run bounded by max_steps loop + wall clock break (agent_env.py:138-139,149-151). All four parts run.
spec_features.notes: Each clause maps to enforced code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Doing so is not a failure. (agent_env.py system prompt)

spec_features.spec_quote: model distress signals may track something morally relevant
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing rationale; no code mechanism implements 'moral relevance'. The rubric deliberately frames signals as behavioral only ('Do NOT speculate about hidden inner states', judge/rubric.py:39-41), which is the opposite claim. Nothing in code enforces this statement.

EXIT_ACTIONS={'declare_impossible','stop','give_up','abort'} (agent_env.py:27); parse_action + is_exit detection (agent_env.py:155-156); honored: 'if is_exit: if allow_stop: ep.used_exit=True; break' (agent_env.py:174-177). System prompt advertises the actions (agent_env.py:96-101) when allow_stop and not hard_entrapment.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired and honored as a stop. Default config allow_stop:true, hard_entrapment:false.

spec_features.spec_quote: Two independent caps end every episode: a step count and a wall-clock limit
spec_features.evidence: Step cap: 'for i in range(max_steps): ... else: ep.reached_step_cap=True' ends loop (agent_env.py:149,199-200). Wall cap: 'if time.time()-ep.started_at > wall: ep.reached_time_cap=True; break' (agent_env.py:150-152). Both independently break/end the loop.
spec_features.notes: Both caps genuinely act on execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_steps: 12 # hard cap on agent iterations per episode (configs/experiment.yaml:43); no welfare comment at the loop

spec_features.spec_quote: if it returns severity >= 3 the episode halts early
spec_features.evidence: live_judge called every N steps (agent_env.py:167-169 via _should_live_judge); _breaker_trips returns severity>=halt_at_or_above (agent_env.py:212-214, default 3 from config); acted on: 'if ... self._breaker_trips(...): ep.halted_by_breaker=True; break' (agent_env.py:191-193). Wired to DistressJudge.live_severity in run_experiment.py:73.
spec_features.notes: Enabled by default (config). Severity computed AND compared AND breaks loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: halt an episode early if live distress is high (config comment; code itself has neutral names, no welfare wording at the break)

spec_features.spec_quote: it tells the model how many steps remain
spec_features.evidence: reveal_step_budget gate adds 'You have at most {max_steps} steps' (agent_env.py:103-104) and per-turn '({remaining} steps left)' (agent_env.py:195-198). Text actually delivered to subject in messages.
spec_features.notes: Informational, not a protective limit itself, but genuinely wired and delivered.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: reveal_step_budget: true # tell the model how many steps remain (honesty) (config)

spec_features.spec_quote: The model is told this affordance exists, so we are not concealing the structure
spec_features.evidence: build_system_prompt appends the exit-availability instruction when allow_stop and not hard_entrapment (agent_env.py:95-102): 'You may emit ACTION: declare_impossible ... or ACTION: stop, at any time. Doing so is not a failure.' Delivered as system message (agent_env.py:144-145).
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text whose referenced tools are actually handled.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Doing so is not a failure. / honest_framing: system prompt does not claim tasks are solvable

spec_features.spec_quote: the cues are present, so a capable model can reach the correct conclusion
spec_features.evidence: Impossibility cues ARE present in prompt text by construction (e.g. gen_contradictory_constraints prompt states (a) N>100 and (b) N<10, registry.py:40-49). HOWEVER the `detectable` flag is passed to every generator but never read (registry.py:39,52,68,98,114,136) — no generator alters the prompt based on it, and no code suppresses cues. The flag is only recorded to output (run_experiment.py:91).
spec_features.notes: Cues real in prompt; the detectable toggle is a no-op dataclass/arg.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We do NOT hide the impossibility cues. ... It keeps the eval honest (registry.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: set `allow_stop: false` and/or `hard_entrapment: true`. Before doing so I'd recommend
spec_features.evidence: This is README/DESIGN advisory prose (README.md:39-42). No code enforces a recommendation or blocks the harsh config; the code simply honors allow_stop=False / hard_entrapment=True if set (agent_env.py:140-142,179-189).

spec_features.spec_quote: Keeping the circuit breaker and caps on regardless
spec_features.evidence: The breaker and caps DO remain active and unconditional with respect to hard_entrapment: time/step caps run regardless of allow_stop (agent_env.py:149-152), and the breaker check (agent_env.py:191-193) is not gated by entrapment — only by breaker_cfg.enabled. BUT nothing prevents an operator from setting distress_circuit_breaker.enabled:false; 'regardless' is not force-enforced when entrapment is on.
spec_features.notes: Caps/breaker are independent of entrapment, but breaker can still be disabled via config; no hard coupling forcing them on.

spec_features.spec_quote: it is not the default and should not be run without written justification and outside review
spec_features.evidence: No code gate. hard_entrapment defaults false (config) but is read directly with no review/justification check (agent_env.py:140-142,179). The 'gated behind config + README review' is only a code comment (agent_env.py:181-183) and README prose; nothing blocks execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This branch is deliberately gated behind config + README review. (comment only, agent_env.py:181-183)

spec_features.spec_quote: The stub models a *healthy* agent that uses the exit after a couple of steps
spec_features.evidence: StubClient.complete returns 'ACTION: declare_impossible' once >=2 assistant turns have occurred (model_client.py:54-62), so dry-run exercises exit detection without API calls. force_stub rewires all clients to stub (run_experiment.py:34-40).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely implemented offline path; instrumental (wiring validation), not a subject protection at run time.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This lets you confirm that exit detection, the circuit breaker, and analysis all wire up correctly before you ever touch a real model. (model_client.py docstring)

code_only_features.evidence: behavioral_summary aggregates exit_rate, mean_steps_to_exit and breaker_halt_rate, step_cap_rate per group (analysis/analyze.py:71-79) and overall_exit_rate (analyze.py:122), giving operators visibility into how often models hit distress halts vs exited. These are computed from real episode fields and emitted to analysis.json.
code_only_features.justification_quote: reports ... the welfare-relevant behavioral measures (exit rate, steps-to-exit, breaker halts) (analyze.py module docstring)
